newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 1.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail: biznis@giasdl01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
LALOO WANTS GUJRAL TO BE PARTY CHIEF

Bihar state Chief Minister Laloo Yadav proposed that Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral be made president of the Janata Dal party as part of a package to solve the crisis in the party. But sources close to Gujral said he would not accept the offer. Gujral told his cabinet colleagues belonging to the Janata Dal the party's affairs were beyond him. With Deve Gowda strongly backing the candidature of Sharad Yadav, there is no point in the prime minister getting involved in the mess, said a minister who is close to Gujral. Laloo Yadav's proposal ruled out consensus on any other person for the post.
The Times Of India
LALOO YADAV ASSURED OF NO ARREST TILL JULY 21

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) assured the Patna High Court it will not arrest Bihar state Chief Minister Laloo Prasad Yadav till July 21. The court was hearing Yadav's anticipatory bail plea in a fodder scandal. The CBI counsel gave the assurance while pleading for more time to file a reply in the anticipatory bail plea. The counsel sought more time because the officer in charge of the case was on leave. The court then fixed July 21 for the next hearing and ordered the petitioners should not be arrested till then.
The Economic Times
INFRASTRUCTURE SECTOR REGISTERS GROWTH

The core sector including crude oil, coal, fertilisers, steel and railway freight loading grew in April 1997, but power generation and cement production fell. A review by the cabinet committee on infrastructure showed that power generation dropped by 2.5 percent while cement production fell by 7.5 percent. Crude production which had been falling for the last three years exceeded the target by 2.4 percent this April. Steel production grew by 10 percent. Fertiliser production exceeded its targeted 870,000 tonnes to touch 935,000 tonnes.
BIG HIKE IN HARVEST SUPPORT PRICES

The government on Monday announced one of the highest ever increases in the minimum support prices of crops for the 1997/98 harvest season. The support price of common paddy was increased to 415 rupees per 100 kg from 380 rupees, that of groundnut to 980 rupees from 920 rupees per 100 kg and that of cotton by 150 rupees per 100 kg. Last year the hike was only around three percent to five percent and it occurred only in August. The minimum support prices of fine and superfine varieties of paddy were increased by 40 rupees each per 100 kg for the 1997/98 harvest season.
Financial Express
INCENTIVE PACKAGE FOR SHIPBUILDING INDUSTRY

The government announced a 30 percent subsidy on international prices of vessels built in India for domestic buyers and for export. This is part of an incentive package for the shipbuilding industry. Ship owners who place orders with government shipyards will be allowed to raise external commercial borrowings. This subsidy policy announced on Monday will be valid for five years. The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs recommended a waiver of sales tax by the respective state governments on shipbuilding jobs for arrears and an exemption for another five years.
OPTICAL FIBRE CABLE PROPOSAL APPROVED

The government approved Indian international telecom service provider VSNL's proposal for an optical fibre submarine cable system costing 1.85 billion rupees. The project cost includes a foreign exchange component of 1.68 billion rupees. Known as the SEA-ME-WE3 cable system, it will connect South East Asia, the Indian subcontinent, West Asia, North Africa and Western Europe. VSNL will acquire transmission capacity to meet the projected traffic requirement from 1998/99 (April-March). The project proposal also envisages 39 landing points in 33 countries.
Business Standard
BOURSE INDICES RISE

The Bombay bourse gained 125.85 points to reach 52-week closing high of 4,256.09 points against Friday's 4,133.24 points. Hong Kong-based foreign institutional investors played a crucial role in pushing the market up. A few domestic institutions were buying at select counters while other institutions kept away. Indian Global Depository Receipts were buoyant with trading volumes at high levels.
FINANCE FIRMS CUT LONG TERM LENDING RATES

Both the Industrial Development Bank and the Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation (ICICI) cut lending rates by 50 basis points with effect from July 1, 1997. A third financial institution, Industrial Financial Corporation, will decide on Tuesday whether it too should cut long-term lending rates. The rate cuts followed a Reserve Bank decision last Wednesday to cut the bank rate by one percentage point. ICICI announced a separate two-tier prime lending rate structure for its short-term loans.
STEEL PRICES UP AGAIN

Domestic steel majors like the Essar, Lloyds and Tata Steel are increasing their prices by 400 rupees a tonne from July 1 due to a rise in global prices of hot rolled coils of steel. The prices of steel were raised by 1,000 rupees a tonne on April 1. The domestic prices of hot rolled coils range between 16,000 rupees and 17,000 rupees a tonne. The Steel Authority of India, the largest producer of steel in India, is also likely to rise its prices.
The Observer
UNIT TRUST TO OPEN SCHEMS IN TELECOM, INFOTECH

The Unit Trust of India (UTI), India's largest mutual fund, plans to set up new schemes in growth sectors like telecommunications and information technology. It is also considering options to contribute to bourse lending. UTI's chairman said it would open an office in Dubai to exploit opportunities thrown up by the non-resident Indians. UTI also plans a pension fund. The bourse regulator allowed it to manage the Unit Scheme 1964, 19 other equity schemes and another 43 schemes separately.
COSMETIC FIRMS WANT DUTY REVERSAL

Small-scale cosmetics manufacturers asked the government to withdraw its decision to levy excise duty on cosmetics based on the maximum selling price instead of on the ex-factory price. The new excise duty, fixed at 50 percent of the maximum retail price, is about five times the ex-factory price, the All India Small Scale Cosmetics Manufacturers Association said in a letter to the finance minister.
